mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate indicates monetary easing, which can lead to increased borrowing and investment, thereby driving up S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following a federal funds rate decline, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate suggests a weakening labor market, which could negatively impact consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to lower S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases by >0.2pp in one month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 20-day windows following an unemployment rate increase, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts indicates stronger demand in the housing market, which can lead to increased economic activity and higher S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >5% in one month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 30% of the 60-day windows following a housing starts increase, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising employment and rising unemployment rate suggests labor market inefficiencies, which could lead to economic instability and lower S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following a rise in both employment and unemployment rate, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production indicates stronger economic output, which can lead to higher S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 30% of the 60-day windows following an increase in industrial production, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of high federal funds rate and rising unemployment rate suggests tight monetary conditions, which can lead to lower S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and UNRATE increases by >0.2pp in one month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following high federal funds rate and rising unemployment, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real consumer spending suggests stronger demand, which can lead to higher S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases by >1% in one month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 50% of the 5-day windows following a real consumer spending increase, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low unemployment rate and high federal funds rate suggests inflationary pressures, which can lead to lower S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: low unemployment with high interest rates
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of the 60-day windows following low unemployment and high federal funds rate, the hypothesis is rejected.
